title: Why we test on held-out data

items.stem: Why shouldn't you measure a model's accuracy on the same data you trained it on?

options.text: You can, as long as the training data is large enough
The model has already learned from that data, so the score is too optimistic
The model forgets the training data once training is finished

items.stem: You have a dataset of 1,000 rows and use an 80/20 train/test split. How many rows are in the test set?
In one sentence, what does a model's test score estimate?
You check the test accuracy after every change to your model and keep the version with the best test score. What is the problem?

options.text: Nothing, that is what the test set is for
The training accuracy will go down
The test set is no longer unseen, so its score becomes too optimistic

items.stem: Why must the test rows be kept out of training?
A model has 99% training accuracy and 70% test accuracy. Which number tells you how it will do on new data?
